questions.q: A coil of negligible resistance is connected in series with $90 \Omega$ resistor across $120 \mathrm{~V}, 60 \mathrm{~Hz}$ supply. A voltmeter reads $36 \mathrm{~V}$ across resistance. Inductance of the coil is :

questions.q: When a $d c$ voltage of $100 \mathrm{~V}$ is applied to an inductor, a $d c$ current of $5 \mathrm{~A}$ flows through it. When an ac voltage of $200 \mathrm{~V}$ peak value is connected to inductor, its inductive reactance is found to be $20 \sqrt{3} \Omega$. The power dissipated in the circuit is _______ W.
questions.solution:
For DC voltage
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{I}}=\frac{100}{5}=20 \Omega$
for AC voltage
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=20 \sqrt{3} \Omega \\
& \mathrm{R}=20 \Omega \\
& \mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2+\mathrm{R}^2}=\sqrt{3 \times 400+400}=40 \Omega \\
& \text { Power }=\mathrm{i}_{\text {rms }}^2 \mathrm{R} \\
& \quad=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\text {rms }}}{\mathrm{Z}}\right)^2 \times \mathrm{R}=\left(\frac{\frac{200}{\sqrt{2}}}{40}\right)^2 \times 20=250 \mathrm{~W}
\end{aligned}$

$= 36\muC$

questions.q: The primary side of a transformer is connected to $230V, 50Hz$ supply. The turn ratio of primary to secondary winding is $10: 1$. Load resistance connected to the secondary side is $46Ω$. The power consumed in it is:
questions.solution:
The voltages associated with the primary and the secondary side of the transformer are related to the turn ratio as follows:

$\dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{V}_{2}} = \dfrac{{N}_{1}}{{N}_{2}} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$\dfrac{230}{{V}_{2}} = \dfrac{10}{1}$

${V}_{2} = 23V$

Hence, the power consumed can be calculated as follows

$\begin{cases}P & = & {V}_{2}^{2}R \\ & = & \dfrac{23 \times 23}{46} \\ & = & 11 . 5W\end{cases}$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $12.5 \mathrm{pF}$ is charged by a battery connected between its plates to potential difference of $12.0 \mathrm{~V}$. The battery is now disconnected and a dielectric slab $\left(\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=6\right)$ is inserted between the plates. The change in its potential energy after inserting the dielectric slab is _____ $10^{-12} \mathrm{~J}$.
questions.solution:
Before inserting dielectric capacitance is given $\mathrm{C}_0=12.5 \mathrm{pF}$ and charge on the capacitor $\mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}$ After inserting dielectric capacitance will become $\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{C}_0$. Change in potential energy of the capacitor $\begin{aligned} & =\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{i}}}-\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{f}}}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_0}\left[1-\frac{1}{\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}\right] \\ & =\frac{\left(\mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}\right)^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_0}\left[1-\frac{1}{\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}\right]=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}^2\left[1-\frac{1}{\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}\right] \end{aligned}$
Using $\mathrm{C}_0=12.5 \mathrm{pF}, \mathrm{V}=12 \mathrm{~V}, \epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=6$ $\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}(12.5) \times 12^2\left[1-\frac{1}{6}\right]=\frac{1}{2}(12.5) \times 12^2 \times \frac{5}{6} \\ & =750 \mathrm{pJ}=750 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~J} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Three capacitors of capacitances $25 \mu \mathrm{F}, 30 \mu \mathrm{F}$ and $45 \mu \mathrm{F}$ are connected in parallel to a supply of $100 \mathrm{~V}$. Energy stored in the above combination is E. When these capacitors are connected in series to the same supply, the stored energy is $\frac{9}{x} \mathrm{E}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
In parallel combination : Potential difference is same across all
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Energy }=\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2+\mathrm{C}_3\right) \mathrm{V}^2 \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(25+30+45) \times(100)^2 \times 10^{-6}=0.5=\mathrm{E}
\end{aligned}$
In series combination: Charge is same on all.
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_3}=\frac{1}{25}+\frac{1}{30}+\frac{1}{45} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}}=\frac{(18+15+10)}{450}=\frac{43}{450} \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}=\frac{450}{43} \\
& \text { Energy }=\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_1}+\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_2}+\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_3} \\
& =\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2}\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_2}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_3}\right] \\
& \frac{\left(\mathrm{V} \times \mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}\right)^2}{2} \times \frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^2 \mathrm{C}_{\text {equ }}}{2} \\
& \frac{(100)^2}{2} \times \frac{450}{43} \times 10^{-6} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{4.5}{86}=\frac{9}{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{E}=\frac{9}{\mathrm{x}} \times 0.5 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=86
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A $16Ω$ wire is bend to form a square loop. A $9V$ battery with internal resistance $1Ω$ is connected across one of its sides. If a $4\mu F$ capacitor is connected across one of its diagonals, the energy stored by the capacitor will be $\dfrac{x}{2}\mu J$, where $x =$______.
questions.solution:
Under the balanced state, there is no flow of charge through the capacitor. So, the path connecting the capacitor behaves as an open path.

The equivalent resistance of the entire circuit, under equilibrium condition, can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}{R}_{eq} & = & 1 + \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{4 + 4 + 4} + \dfrac{1}{4}}Ω \\ & = & \left(1 + 3\right)Ω \\ & = & 4Ω\end{cases}$

Hence, the current through the entire circuit is given by

$\begin{cases}I & = & \dfrac{V}{{R}_{eq}} \\ & = & \dfrac{9}{4}A\end{cases}$

So, the current $\left({I}_{1}\right)$ can be written as

$\begin{cases}{I}_{1} & = & \dfrac{9}{4} \times \dfrac{4}{16}A \\ & = & \dfrac{9}{16}A\end{cases}$

The potential difference between the points $A$ and $B$ is,

$\begin{cases}{V}_{A} - {V}_{B} & = & {I}_{1} \times 8 \\ & = & \dfrac{9}{16} \times 8 \\ & = & \dfrac{9}{2}V\end{cases}$

Hence, the energy stored in the capacitor is given by

$\begin{cases}U & = & \dfrac{1}{2}C{\left({V}_{A} - {V}_{B}\right)}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times \dfrac{81}{4}\mu J \\ & = & \dfrac{81}{2}\mu J\end{cases}$

$∴ x = 81$

$\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{g}}=\frac{10}{400+100}=20 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~A}$
For ammeter
Let shunt resistance $=\mathrm{S}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{g}} \mathrm{R}=\left(\mathrm{i}-\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{g}}\right) \mathrm{S} \\
& 20 \times 10^{-3} \times 100=10 \mathrm{~S} \\
& \mathrm{~S}=20 \times 10^{-2} \Omega
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two coils have mutual inductance $0 . 002H$. The current changes in the first coil according to the relation $i = {i}_{0}sin\omegat$, where ${i}_{0} = 5A$ and $\omega = 50\pi$ $rad{s}^{- 1}$. The maximum value of $emf$ in the second coil is $\dfrac{\pi}{\alpha}V$. The value of $\alpha$ is
questions.solution:
The amount of flux induced in the second coil due to the first one is given by

$\begin{cases}{ϕ}_{2} & = & Mi \\ & = & M{i}_{0}sin\omegat . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

where, $M$ is the mutual inductance of the coils.

The formula to calculate the emf induced can be written as

$ε = - \dfrac{d{ϕ}_{2}}{dt} . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation (2), it follows that,

$\begin{cases}{ε}_{max} & = & M{i}_{0}\omega \\ & = & 0 . 002 \times 5 \times 50\piV \\ & = & \dfrac{\pi}{2}V\end{cases}$

Hence, $\alpha = 2$.

questions.q: A square loop of side $10cm$ and resistance $0 . 7Ω$ is placed vertically in the east-west plane. A uniform magnetic field of $0 . 20T$ is set up across the plane in the north-east direction. The magnetic field is decreased to zero in $1s$ at a steady rate. Then, the magnitude of induced emf is $\sqrt{x} \times {10}^{- 3}V$. The value of $x$ is _______.
questions.solution:
The area vector for the square loop is given by

$\overset{\to}{A} = ( 0 . 1{)}^{2}\overset{^}{j}{m}^{2}$

According to the above diagram, the magnetic field is given by

$\overset{\to}{B} = \dfrac{0 . 2}{\sqrt{2}}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{0 . 2}{\sqrt{2}}\overset{^}{j}$

Hence, the magnitude of induced emf can be calculated as follows

$\begin{cases}e & = & \dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{\Deltat} \\ & = & \dfrac{\overset{\to}{B} \cdot \overset{\to}{A} - 0}{1} \\ & = & \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{0 . 2}{\sqrt{2}}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{0 . 2}{\sqrt{2}}\overset{^}{j}\right) \cdot \left(( 0 . 1{)}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) - 0}{1}V \\ & = & \sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 3}V\end{cases}$

Hence, $x = 2$.

questions.q: A rectangular loop of sides $12cm$ and $5cm$, with its sides parallel to the $x$-axis and $y$-axis respectively moves with a velocity of $5cm{s}^{- 1}$ in the positive $x$ axis direction, in a space containing a variable magnetic field in the positive $z$ direction. The field has a gradient of ${10}^{- 3}T{cm}^{- 1}$ along the negative $x$ direction and it is decreasing with time at the rate of ${10}^{- 3}T{s}^{- 1} .$ If the resistance of the loop is $6mΩ$, the power dissipated by the loop as heat is ______ $\times {10}^{- 9}W .$
questions.solution:
Let ${B}_{0}$ is the magnetic field at origin. Then,

$\dfrac{dB}{dx} = - \dfrac{{10}^{- 3}}{{10}^{- 2}}$

$⇒ {∫}_{{B}_{0}}^{B}dB = - {∫}_{0}^{x}{10}^{- 1}dx$

$⇒ B - {B}_{0} = - {10}^{- 1}x$

$⇒ B = \left({B}_{0} - \dfrac{x}{10}\right)$

Motional emf in $AB = 0$

Motional emf in $CD = 0$

Motional emf in $AD = {ε}_{1} = {B}_{0}ℓv$

Magnetic field on rod $BC$ 

$= \left({B}_{0} - \dfrac{\left(- 12 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}{10}\right)$

Motional emf in  $BC = {ε}_{2} = \left({B}_{0} + \dfrac{12 \times {10}^{- 2}}{10}\right)ℓ \times v$

Net equivalent emf ${ε}_{eq} = {ε}_{2} - {ε}_{1} = 300 \times {10}^{- 7}V$

For time variation

${\left({ε}_{eq}\right)}^{'} = A\dfrac{dB}{dt} = 60 \times {10}^{- 7}V$

${\left({ε}_{eq}\right)}_{\text{net}} = {ε}_{eq} + {\left({ε}_{eq}\right)}^{'} = 360 \times {10}^{- 7}V$

Power $r = {\left({ε}_{\text{eq}}\right)}_{\text{net}}^{2}R = 216 \times {10}^{- 9}W$

questions.q: A small square loop of wire of side $l$ is placed inside a large square loop of wire of side $L$$\left(L = {l}^{2}\right)$. The loops are coplanar and their centers coincide. The value of the mutual inductance of the system is $\sqrt{x} \times {10}^{- 7}H$, where $x =$______.
questions.solution:
Flux linkage for inner loop

$ϕ = {B}_{center} \times {l}^{2}$

$= 4 \times \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\pi\dfrac{L}{2}}\left(sin45 ° + sin45 °\right){l}^{2}$

$⇒ ϕ = 2\sqrt{2}\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{\piL}{l}^{2}$

Therefore, mutual inductance will be

$M = \dfrac{ϕ}{i} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}{\mu}_{0}{l}^{2}}{\piL} = 2\sqrt{2}\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{\pi}$

$= 2\sqrt{2}\dfrac{4\pi}{\pi} \times {10}^{- 7}$

$= 8\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 7}$

$= \sqrt{128} \times {10}^{- 7}H$

Hence, $x = 128$.

questions.q: An infinitely long positively charged straight thread has a linear charge density $\lambda \mathrm{Cm}^{-1}$. An electron revolves along a circular path having axis along the length of the wire. The graph that correctly represents the variation of the kinetic energy of electron as a function of radius of circular path from the wire is :
questions.solution:
Electric field $\mathrm{E}$ at a distance $\mathrm{r}$ due to infinite long wire is $E=\frac{2 k \lambda}{r}$ Force of electron $\Rightarrow F=e E$ $\begin{aligned} & F=e\left(\frac{2 k \lambda}{r}\right) \\ & F=\frac{2 k \lambda e}{r} \end{aligned}$
This force will provide required centripetal force $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{F} & =\frac{\mathrm{m}^2}{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{r}} \\ \mathrm{v} & =\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}} \\ \mathrm{KE} & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}\right) \\ & =\mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: When a coil is connected across a $20 \mathrm{~V}$ dc supply, it draws a current of $5 \mathrm{~A}$. When it is connected across $20 \mathrm{~V}, 50 \mathrm{~Hz}$ ac supply, it draws a current of $4 \mathrm{~A}$. The self inductance of the coil is ______ $\mathrm{mH}$. $($ Take $\pi=3$ )
questions.solution:
Case-I:
$i=\frac{20}{R} \Rightarrow R=4 \Omega$ Case-II:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{i}=\frac{20}{\mathrm{Z}} \\ & 4=\frac{20}{\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2}=5 \\ & \mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2=25 \Rightarrow \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=3 \Omega \\ & \mathrm{L}=\frac{3}{2 \pi \mathrm{f}}=\frac{1}{2 \times 50}=\frac{1000}{100} \mathrm{mH} \\ & \mathrm{L}=10 \mathrm{mH}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An electron is moving under the influence of the electric field of a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet $S$ having surface charge density $+ \sigma$. The electron at $t = 0$ is at a distance of $1m$ from $S$ and has a speed of $1m{s}^{- 1}$. The maximum value of $\sigma$, if the electron strikes $S$ at $t = 1s$ is $\alpha\left[\dfrac{m{ϵ}_{0}}{e}\right]\dfrac{C}{{m}^{2}}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The value of the electric field due to the uniformly charged plane sheet is given by

$E = \dfrac{\sigma}{2{ε}_{0}} . . . \left(1\right)$

Thus, the force on the electron is given by

$\begin{cases}F & = & - eE \\ & = & - \dfrac{\sigmae}{2{ε}_{0}} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

So, the acceleration of the electron is given by

$a = - \dfrac{\sigmae}{2{ε}_{0}m}$

Given, $u = 1m{s}^{- 1}$, $t = 1s$ and $S = - 1m$

Using the equation of motion, it can be written that

$- 1 = 1 \times 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{\sigmae}{2{ε}_{0}m} \times ( 1{)}^{2} ⇒ \sigma = 8\dfrac{{ε}_{0}m}{e}C{m}^{- 2}$

$∴ \alpha = 8$.

questions.q: Two identical charged spheres are suspended by strings of equal lengths. The string make an angle of $37 °$ with each other. When suspended in a liquid of density $0 . 7g{cm}^{- 3}$, the angle remains same. If density of material of the sphere is $1 . 4g{cm}^{- 3}$, the dielectric constant of the liquid is _____ $\left(tan37 ° = \dfrac{3}{4}\right)$
questions.solution:
For first case:

$Tcos\theta = mg$ and 

$Tsin\theta = {F}_{e}$

Therefore, $tan\theta = \dfrac{{F}_{e}}{mg}$

$tan\theta = \dfrac{{F}_{e}}{{ρ}_{B}Vg} . . . . ( i )$

For second case:

$tan\theta = \dfrac{\dfrac{{F}_{e}}{k}}{{ρ}_{B}Vg - {ρ}_{L}Vg} . . . . . ( ii )$ 

From Eq. (i) & (ii), we get

${ρ}_{B}Vg = \left({ρ}_{B} - {ρ}_{L}\right)kVg$

$⇒ 1 . 4 = 0 . 7k$

$⇒ k = 2$

A square loop of edge $50 \mathrm{~cm}$ carrying 0.5 A current is placed in $x-y$ plane with its edges parallel to the $x-y$ axes, as shown in figure. Force on segment parallel to $\mathrm{x}$-axis will cancel each other. Hence $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{net}}$ will be due to portion parallel to $y$-axis.

& =0.5 \times 0.5 \times 0.2 \\
& =0.25 \times 0.2 \\
& =50 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~N} \\
& =50 \mathrm{mN}
\end{aligned}$

A thin metallic wire having cross sectional area of ${10}^{- 4}{m}^{2}$ is used to make a ring of radius $30cm$. A positive charge of $2\piC$ is uniformly distributed over the ring, while another positive charge of $30pC$ is kept at the centre of the ring. The tension in the ring is $_______N$; provided that the ring does not get deformed (neglect the influence of gravity).

(Given, $\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}$ SI units)
questions.solution:
The linear charge density of the ring is given by

$\lambda = \dfrac{Q}{2\piR} . . . \left(1\right)$

With reference to the above diagram, for the equilibrium condition of the ring, it can be written that

$2Tsin\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{{q}_{0}}{{R}^{2}} \cdot \left[\lambda\left(Rd\theta\right)\right]$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{{q}_{0}Q}{\left({R}^{2}\right) \times 2\pi}$ [As for very small angles $sin\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{d\theta}{2}$]

$= \dfrac{\left(9 \times {10}^{9}\right)\left(2\pi \times 30 \times {10}^{- 12}\right)}{( 0 . 30{)}^{2} \times 2\pi}$

$= \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 30}{9 \times {10}^{- 2}} = 3N$

questions.q: A circular coil having 200 turns, $2.5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2$ area and carrying $100 \mu \mathrm{A}$ current is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 1T. Initially the magnetic dipole moment $(\vec{M})$ was directed along $\vec{B}$. questions.q: Two long, straight wires carry equal currents in opposite directions as shown in figure. The separation between the wires is $5 . 0cm$. The magnitude of the magnetic field at a point $P$ midway between the wires is $_____\muT$. (Given: ${\mu}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}Tm{A}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
The direction of the magnetic field at the observation point due to the current carrying conductor is determined by the right-hand cork screw rule.

From the given diagram, it is clear that as the conductors carry current in the mutually opposite direction, the direction of the magnetic fields produced by them at point $P$ will be the same.

Hence, the required magnetic field at $P$ due to the conductors can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}B & = & 2 \times \left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2\pia}\right) \\ & = & 2 \times \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 10}{2\pi \times \left(\dfrac{5}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}T \\ & = & 160 \times {10}^{- 6}T \\ & = & 160\mu T\end{cases}$

questions.solution:
Right hand thumb rule states that, “If you imagine holding a current carrying wire in your right-hand with your thumb pointing towards the direction of electric current flow then the direction in which your fingers curl, gives the direction of lines of force of the magnetic field”. In this case, direciton of magnetic field at the centre for both wires is as shown below.

Magnetic field due to a circular wire is given by, ${B}_{A} = {B}_{B} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2a}$

As both magnetic field lines at centre are perpendicular, therefore

$∵ {B}_{net} = \sqrt{{\left({B}_{A}\right)}^{2} + {\left({B}_{B}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}{\mu}_{0}I}{2a} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{\sqrt{2}a}$

questions.q:
A proton moving with a constant velocity passes through a region of space without any change in its velocity. If $\overset{ o}{E}$ and $\overset{ o}{B}$ represent the electric and magnetic fields respectively, then the region of space may have :
(A) $E = 0, B = 0$; (B) $E = 0, B e 0$; (C) $E e 0, B = 0$; (D) $E e 0, B e 0$

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Net force on proton inside an electric and a magnetic field is given by

$\overset{ o}{F}e + \overset{ o}{F}m = q\overset{ o}{E} + q\left(\overset{ o}{v} imes \overset{ o}{B} ight) . . . \left(1 ight)$

If both $\overset{ o}{E}$ and $\overset{ o}{B}$ are zero, then $\overset{ o}{F}e$ and $\overset{ o}{F}m$ both are zero. Hence, velocity may remain constant. Therefore, option (A) is correct.

If $E = 0, B e 0$, but velocity is parallel or antiparallel to the magnetic field, then also $\overset{ o}{F}e$ and $\overset{ o}{F}m$ both are zero. Hence, option (B) is also correct.

If $E e 0, B e 0$, but $\overset{ o}{F}e + \overset{ o}{F}m = 0$, then also velocity may remain constant. Thus, option (D) is also correct.

questions.q: A regular polygon of $6$ sides is formed by bending a wire of length $4\pi$ meter. If an electric current of $4\pi\sqrt{3}A$ is flowing through the sides of the polygon, the magnetic field at the centre of the polygon would be $x \times {10}^{- 7}T .$ The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Direction of magnetic field due to all six sides will be in the same direction, therefore we can write 

$B = 6\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pir}\right)\left(sin30 ° + sin30 °\right)$, where $r =$distance of the sides from the centre.

$= 6\dfrac{{10}^{- 7} \times 4\pi\sqrt{3}}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} \times \sqrt{3}\right)}$

$= 72 \times {10}^{- 7}T$

Hence, $x = 72$.

questions.q: The coercivity of a magnet is $5 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{m}$. The amount of current required to be passed in a solenoid of length $30 \mathrm{~cm}$ and the number of turns 150 , so that the magnet gets demagnetised when inside the solenoid is _____A.
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{ni}}{\mu_{\mathrm{o}}} \\ & 5 \times 10^3=\frac{150}{30} \times 100 \times \mathrm{i} \\ & \frac{50}{5}=\mathrm{i} \\ & \mathrm{I}=10\end{aligned}$
